title: Oversized annotation tag values are skipped per-label, not fatal to the batch
answers: Alert history save fails because one label is too long
Why does one oversized label just vanish instead of erroring?
How are over-limit annotation tags handled?
body:
Symptom: a single overly long label (key or value) must not abort saving the whole annotation/history batch.
Root cause: convertLabelsToTagsWithLogger in pkg/services/ngalert/state/historian/annotation.go filters out individual labels exceeding column limits (or the configured total tags length) and logs a warning, continuing with the rest.
Fix pattern: when adding new length/size guards on tags, skip-and-warn per offending label rather than erroring the batch; include labelKey, labelValueLength and maxLabelValueLength in the warn log context, but never log the actual oversized value (PII/size risk).
Constraints: applies to both the per-column limit (annotationTagValueColumnMaxLength) and the separate configured total-tags-length budget passed into convertLabelsToTagsWithLogger; both paths must keep logging only metadata, not raw values.

Log context must include labelKey, labelValueLength, and maxLabelValueLength but never the actual oversized value due to PII and size concerns. This per-label skip-and-continue behavior applies to both per-column and total-tags-length guards.
